title: County of Besalú
capsule: The County of Besalú was a Catalan march county centred on the town of Besalú in what is now the Garrotxa (northeastern Catalonia), separated from the County of Girona in 878 by Wilfred the Hairy, who installed his brother Radulf as its first count. Through the ninth and tenth centuries it was held by Wilfred's Barcelona-Cerdanya kindred, passing through Miró I, Wilfred II, Sunifred, and the cleric-count Miró II Bonfill (965–984), and remained a constituent piece of the broader Catalan comital network rather than an independent power. When Oliba Cabreta withdrew to the monastery of Montecassino in 988, his son Bernard Tallaferro began the line that would later make Besalú a more autonomous county.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The county's core extent is derived from 10th–11th century charters and castle records; its northern boundary into Aude is reasonably well-documented, though the exact frontier fluctuated.
